answer: Behavioral watermark routing. Each identity gets a unique hidden query schedule drawn from a shared river of tasks; answers must carry subtle timing and phrasing marks tied to that schedule. A clone cannot copy them without replaying the original's exact interaction history, which the system cross-checks against a vine of prior sessions. Mismatches flag duplication and freeze the copy. An attacker must either maintain full parallel histories per clone, costing continuous compute and latency per identity, or risk detection when the pattern diverges into a hollow shell.
